cohort: The study included 662 mothers who were interviewed face-to-face during hospital visits in Jashore district, Bangladesh.
finding: The prevalence of cesarean delivery in Jashore district was 70.5%, with significant associations found with socioeconomic factors, type of hospital, obstetric history, and patient/doctor preferences.
mod_finding: The study found a high cesarean delivery prevalence of 70.5%, which was significantly predicted by rural residence, younger maternal age, nuclear family structure, husbands' occupation, private hospital deliveries, previous CD, maternal self-preference, and doctor's influence.
